author: Dex+others
quote: Do not outsource the thinking
claim: Six-phase QRSPI (Questions, Research, Design, Structure, Plan, Implement) puts a human checkpoint at every phase so the agent shows what it is wrong about before implementation.
evidence_detail: Product copy; no data. Phases described in one line each.
landing: Compare to the 40-phase routine's structure; a questions-first step and a design-doc review before the plan.

author: Dex+others
quote: Catch mistakes before 2,000 lines of code.
claim: Review comments on a design doc, with decisions feeding back to the agent, catch errors earlier than reviewing code.
evidence_detail: Copy; mockup of a design review shown.
landing: Owner review at design/plan artefact (PR 'Plan @ sha' body) rather than only at the end; keep decisions journal as the feedback channel.

author: Dex+others
quote: What we are not doing
claim: The design doc template includes Current State, Desired End State and an explicit 'what we are not doing' list.
evidence_detail: Seen in the mockup design doc only.
landing: Plan template section for the PR body: explicit out-of-scope list per phase.

author: Dex+others
quote: Compounding Engineering — Agents get smarter over time
claim: Pro tier advertises compounding engineering (agents improve with use) and a 'workflow preview' of staged sessions with a per-task artifact set (research.md, design.md, structure.md, plan.md).
evidence_detail: Feature bullet only.
landing: Per-task artifact folder convention (research, design, plan) and reviewed memory feeding future runs; relates to the knowledge-store design.

author: Dex+others
quote: making the prompts and workflows "squishy" - that is, flexible to a broad range of problems
claim: Opinionated workflows are tuned to be flexible to varied inputs so there is no holding it wrong, after hundreds of hours with customers.
evidence_detail: FAQ copy; no data.
landing: Workflow library design: parameterised, tolerant of different task shapes rather than one script per task.

author: Dex+others
quote: You can’t do advanced context engineering without staying in touch with your context.
claim: Full visibility into every thinking message and subagent call is needed to do context engineering.
evidence_detail: Copy.
landing: Observability of sessions (transcripts/evidence folders) as the basis for knowing whether the routine was followed; re-opens the measurement pipeline skipped item.

author: Dex+others
quote: Execute with continuous feedback. No 2,000-line surprises.
claim: Implementation runs against a phased, verifiable structure outline with file paths, test cases and acceptance criteria written first.
evidence_detail: Phase descriptions Structure and Plan.
landing: Plan must name file paths, tests and acceptance criteria per phase; fits the 'fail-before/pass-after per register id' reviewer demand.

author: Dex
quote: Using conditional XML blocks to make Claude pay attention to the right instructions at the right time.

author: Dex
quote: many teams learned the hard way that agents can't be trusted

evidence_detail: Narrative history in an abstract; no numbers.

author: Dex+others
quote: a task started on a directory now runs in its own worktrees instead of editing your checkout
claim: Tasks now run in their own worktrees by default (with an opt-out), and the daemon hides its .shadow folder from git so agents do not commit it.
evidence_detail: Changelog line.

author: Dex+others
quote: CONTRIBUTING.md lists every check a pull request must pass.
claim: The root README is human onboarding only, points to CONTRIBUTING for the PR checks, and keeps agent instructions in a separate AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md is a byte-identical copy) with human-only setup in HUMANS.md.
evidence_detail: File layout of the repo: README, HUMANS.md, AGENTS.md identical to CLAUDE.md.
landing: CLAUDE.md split: audience-specific files and a single source for the agent file

author: Dex
quote: Only use when the user explicitly invokes this skill by name.
claim: The rpi skill description disables model auto-triggering so the workflow only runs when the human names it.
evidence_detail: One-line description in SKILL.md frontmatter; no data.
landing: .claude/skills/ frontmatter for phase-heavy skills

also.quote: Only use when the user explicitly invokes this skill by name.
also.author: Dex+others
also.claim: Nearly all RPI skills use this one description so the model never auto-selects them; the workflow is a fixed sequence the human triggers, and skill bodies are deterministic step lists, not discovery prompts.

author: Dex
quote: read the subagent instructions from $SKILLBASE/references/subagents/SUBAGENT_NAME.md
claim: Skills carry a conditional fallback: if no subagent tool exists, or the named agents are missing, the parent reads a mirrored agent file and either follows it inline or pastes it into a generic subagent prompt.
evidence_detail: Two `<important if>` blocks in SKILL.md; the tests 'fallback-without-delegation', 'fallback-with-generic-delegation' and 'nested-delegation' check it on Codex.
landing: Agent definitions that must work when custom agents are not registered; portability of .claude/agents/fixflow-explorer.md

author: Dex
quote: <important if="you do not have an Agent() or Task() or other tool for running subagents">
claim: The `<important if>` conditional-block pattern from improve-claude-md is used inside the shipped skill so situational instructions only bind when their condition holds.
evidence_detail: Two such blocks in SKILL.md; README describes improve-claude-md as rewriting CLAUDE.md with these blocks 'to improve instruction adherence'.
landing: CLAUDE.md trim: wrap task-specific invariants in conditional blocks

author: Dex
quote: For a task description with no requested step, start with research questions.
claim: With no step named, the default entry is research questions, and the agent must stop and ask which flow the user wants, waiting for the choice before starting the phase.
evidence_detail: Tested by 'flow-choice': asserts no document is written before the user chooses and that a box-drawing chart is shown.
landing: Phase routine first step: stop-and-ask checkpoint before work

author: Dex
quote: Use box-drawing glyphs, not Mermaid.
claim: Choices shown in chat use a plain-text box-and-line chart rather than Mermaid, because the terminal cannot render Mermaid; Mermaid is kept for documents.
evidence_detail: Chart reference file; test asserts a box-drawing code block and the absence of ```mermaid.
landing: nowhere obvious (owner one-page view formatting)

author: Dex
quote: keep the desired change in the separate request document so research stays objective.
claim: The task is split into a neutral questions file for the researcher and a separate request file holding the desired result, so the research agent never sees what is wanted and cannot bias its findings.
evidence_detail: Phase rule; test 'research-isolation' plants decoy request/PRD files and asserts the research session never opened them.
landing: Cold-resume trial design; fresh-context refuters given questions without the claim under test
inventory_ref: (B) QRSPI talk / Humans in the Loop (research prompts returning opinions); repos: skills

author: Dex
quote: Keep this pass small; the next research session does the full investigation.
claim: The questions phase does only a small locate-and-skim pass, then writes two to seven descriptive questions about what exists, each with a concrete starting pointer such as a package or file.
evidence_detail: Phase step 2-3; examples like 'How does the worker recover queued jobs after a restart?'
landing: Phase 0 / discovery step of each ship-plan phase

author: Dex
quote: Give each agent a bounded, read-only question
claim: Research fans out to two to six read-only subagents on independent areas in parallel, each asked for paths, line references, test patterns and evidence, and the parent waits for all before synthesising.
evidence_detail: Steps 2-4 of create-research; also 'resolve conflicting findings against live code'.
landing: Workflow-tool research fan-out template to save as a reusable workflow

author: Dex
quote: Distinguish tests read from checks run.
claim: Research documents must separate tests merely read from checks actually executed, and any claim that a check passed needs its command and observed result.
evidence_detail: Rule repeated in create-research and iterate-research.
landing: Reviewer rule: fail-before/pass-after per register id must cite command and observed output

author: Dex
quote: A reader should understand the main findings by skimming the headers alone.
claim: Findings headers must assert what is true (e.g. 'Workers restore pending jobs before accepting new work') and sections lead with the finding before citing where it lives.
evidence_detail: Template and process rule; same rule recurs in design discussion, PRD and TDD phases.
landing: Takeaway headers in the one-page owner view, decisions journal and CLAUDE.md sections

author: Dex
quote: Ask for a research question when neither research input is available.
claim: A research phase refuses to start without either a questions document or a direct question; and a standalone research answer ends without a forced next phase.
evidence_detail: Step 1 of create-research; test 'standalone-research' asserts no forced next step and no questions document.
landing: Phase entry preconditions

author: Dex
quote: Only the top-level RPI skill is independently discoverable
claim: One discoverable SKILL.md routes to per-phase process.md files kept as plain references (a test asserts no other SKILL.md exists), so the always-loaded surface is one short router and phases load on demand.
evidence_detail: Router table maps 14 requests to create-/iterate- process files; enforced by test-rpi.ts.
landing: Skill layout: one router SKILL.md plus per-phase reference files; a model for splitting CLAUDE.md sections

author: Dex
quote: Open questions identify behavior that remains to be traced or understood.
claim: The research template mandates an explicit Open Questions section, a per-component Testing Patterns subsection, and a code-reference list stating whether coverage is exhaustive or key files only.
evidence_detail: Template headings: Research Question, Methodology, Summary, Detailed Findings, Code References, Architecture, Open Questions.
landing: Verified-diagnosis record shape in the knowledge-store design

author: Dex
quote: You are a documentarian, not a critic or consultant
claim: Research sub-agents are forbidden to suggest improvements, find bugs, critique or root-cause, only to describe the code as it exists with file:line references, so research output stays objective.
evidence_detail: Repeated 'DO NOT' list across locator, analyzer and pattern-finder; analyzer tools Read/Grep/Glob/Bash, model sonnet.
landing: .claude/agents/fixflow-explorer.md prompt: add an explicit no-opinions, file:line-only contract

author: Dex
quote: Don't read file contents - Just report locations
claim: The locator agent is a find-only role: no Read tool, grouped output by purpose (implementation, tests, config, types, entry points) with directory counts, run on sonnet.
evidence_detail: Frontmatter tools: Grep, Glob, Bash, Skill; description 'Super Grep/Glob/LS tool - use it if you find yourself desiring one of these tools more than once'.
landing: fixflow-explorer (Haiku file locator): tool allow-list without Read, output grouping, call-it-after-two-greps trigger

author: Dex
quote: Include tests - Show existing test patterns
claim: A pattern-finder agent returns working code snippets with file:line plus the matching test pattern for each implementation pattern found, without ranking them.
evidence_detail: Output template shows variants (offset vs cursor pagination) and a Testing Patterns block; 'Don't recommend one pattern over another'.
landing: A second custom agent for slice conventions (router-service-repository, outbox kinds) feeding phase plans

author: Dex
quote: Start with 2-3 well-crafted searches before fetching content
claim: The web researcher agent uses a bounded search budget (2-3 searches, 3-5 pages first), prefers curl on llms.txt and .md/.txt URLs over a fetch tool, and ends with a Gaps or Limitations section.
evidence_detail: Agent body; includes the instruction to avoid browser skills unless the user asks.
landing: Agent for dependency-doc lookups (Expo SDK 52, Railway) with a fixed output shape

author: Dex
quote: structure outline > tdd > prd > design discussion > research > original request
claim: Implementers get a fixed document precedence when documents conflict, with the user's latest instruction overriding all of them.
evidence_detail: Stated in the agent and in implement-outline; tests 'document-precedence' and 'latest-user-direction' assert the cap value from the outline wins (1000) and a later user cap (2000) wins over it.
landing: Ship plan versus CLAUDE.md versus phase brief precedence rule for agents

author: Dex
quote: STOP and think deeply about why the outline can't be followed
claim: On a plan mismatch the implementer must stop and report Expected / Found / Why this matters / How should I proceed, instead of improvising.
evidence_detail: Fixed four-line mismatch report format in the agent file.
landing: Decisions journal entry format for plan deviations in a phase PR

also.quote: Present the issue clearly
also.author: Dex
also.claim: On a plan/reality mismatch the implementer must STOP and present Expected / Found / Why this matters, then ask how to proceed; sub-tasks are used sparingly in implementation.

author: Dex
quote: Read files fully - never use limit/offset parameters
claim: The implementer must read every workflow document and every file in full rather than in chunks, and its progress is recorded in the outline itself (checkboxes and a checkmark on the phase heading).
evidence_detail: Getting Started and Progress Tracking sections; model: inherit, tools include Edit/Write/TodoWrite.
landing: Progress marks in the plan file as a self-reported-compliance record; read-in-full rule for phase brief

author: Dex
quote: do not mark phase title with ✅ until the human confirms manual verification passed
claim: Automated and manual verification are separate checklists; a phase is marked complete only after automated checks pass and any manual checks are human-confirmed, and the agent pauses for the human when manual checks remain.
evidence_detail: Pause message template; tests 'phase-pause-and-resume' and 'automated-only-phases' assert phase 2 does not run before review and that unconfirmed manual checks never get a checkmark.
landing: Phase closing message / owner view: split automated from human-confirmed items

author: Dex
quote: Fix failed checks before marking them passed.
claim: The parent re-reviews the implementer's verification evidence and only the parent ticks validation boxes; by default one phase is delegated at a time, and the user can request a group or all phases run continuously.
evidence_detail: Steps 2-3 of implement-outline: launch the implementer with a short prompt of paths, precedence and scope, and let it read the documents itself.
landing: Orchestrator-implementer split with a short delegation prompt (paths plus precedence, not pasted content)

author: Dex
quote: Users run each phase in a separate context window by default.
claim: Each phase runs in its own context window by default, with the document carrying state; the user may instead continue in place or after compaction.
evidence_detail: Stated as default in SKILL.md and workflow.md; next-step commands say run 'here, after compaction, or in a new session'.
landing: Phase routine in ship plan section 0 (one phase per new chat) - already present

author: Dex
quote: Prefer small end-to-end results that cross the relevant module or service boundaries.
claim: The outline is split into vertical slices, each working and verifiable when it ends (serve a simple result, then add editing, then an error path), rather than horizontal layers.
evidence_detail: Step 4; each phase has result, Change Outline and Validation with Automated vs Manual split; Implementation Overview checklist kept in sync.
landing: Ship-plan phase sizing rule (vertical slice per phase with its own checks)

author: Dex
quote: Describe intent and code shape at the level needed to review the work.
claim: The outline carries file trees, contracts, signatures and pseudocode rather than full code, and the implementer's agent states 'outlines describe intent and signatures' - the plan is a reviewable shape, not the implementation.
evidence_detail: Outline process plus implementer 'Implementation Philosophy'.
landing: Ship-plan phase specs: contract and signature level, with checks listed per phase
inventory_ref: (B) QRSPI talk (outline as reviewable artifact); repos: skills

author: Dex
quote: Present one decision at a time with its options and recommendation, then wait
claim: Design is a one-question-at-a-time interview in the main conversation, with options, tradeoffs and a codebase-grounded recommendation; settled choices move into a Resolved Design Questions section with the rejected alternatives and why.
evidence_detail: Step 5; tests 'fresh-design-decision', 'design-with-settled-choices' check settled choices land in Resolved and open ones stay in Design Questions.
landing: Decisions journal format: decision, rationale, alternatives set aside

author: Dex
quote: Keep this opening short so the interview starts promptly.
claim: A PRD starts as a tiny skeleton (problem drafted, other sections empty), then problem, then success measure, then solution are settled in order, with technical questions parked under Deferred to TDD; the user reads Solution Details whole and approves it.
evidence_detail: Steps 2-5; a measure may be recorded as 'none useful' for small work with the user's agreement.
landing: Success measure per phase in the ship plan; deferred-decision list

author: Dex
quote: with a separate user approval for each.
claim: The technical design is split into System Design (components, contracts, sequences) approved first, then Program Design (call trees, signatures, file-tree changes, test seams) approved separately; a test asserts the second approval is not skipped or the first restarted.
evidence_detail: Steps 3-6; tests 'tdd-interview' and 'fresh-program-design' require at least two approvals and no restart of approved System Design.
landing: Two-gate review (architecture then code shape) before implementation for high-risk phases (money, outbox, lifecycle)

author: Dex
quote: Document patterns to follow with source paths and short examples.
claim: Design documents carry a Patterns to Follow section with source paths and short examples including test seams, so the implementing session copies existing conventions.
evidence_detail: Present in the TDD template and design discussion; the pattern-finder agent feeds it.
landing: Move per-slice conventions out of CLAUDE.md into per-phase Patterns to Follow lists

author: Dex
quote: Reproduce the issue or check the requested change against code and tests.
claim: Feedback handling is reproduce first, ask one targeted question with a recommended approach if behaviour is unclear, add a regression test, and update outline sections whose agreed result changed.
evidence_detail: Five short steps; tests 'implementation-feedback' and 'finished-iteration-needs-feedback' (a finished doc without feedback prompts for it instead of editing).
landing: Refuter/reviewer fail-before/pass-after requirement for each register id

author: Dex
quote: Don't say "it", "that", and similar words unless the referent is obvious.
claim: A shared prose reference imposes Orwell's six rules, direct-answer-first brevity, real names for things instead of invented labels, and no unclear pronoun referents, for responses, docs, commit messages and PR descriptions.
evidence_detail: Short file added Oct 31; loaded after each document is written.
landing: Writing rules for closing message, PR body and decisions journal; a skill loaded on write

author: Dex
quote: Pick the smallest view that makes the key point clear.
claim: Explain with the smallest suitable visual (pseudocode, call tree, component tree, shallow file tree, Mermaid, diff) and show change as a diff block rather than prose, using a full block only when most is new.
evidence_detail: Catalogue of six view types with examples; ends with 'don't overwhelm the user'.
landing: Reviewer and owner-view format: diff or call-tree instead of narrative

also.quote: Skip the preamble and keep prose brief. Pick the smallest view that makes the key point clear.
also.author: Dex
also.claim: To explain code, prefer compact structural views (pseudocode, call tree, component tree, file tree, Mermaid, diff) over prose, choosing the smallest view that answers the question.

author: Dex
quote: write one focused HTML file
claim: For dense UI or concept comparisons the agent writes one focused HTML file (diagram, infographic or short deck) in the product's own palette with real labels and opens it, and saves mockups beside the document as ordinary local links.
evidence_detail: Last bullet of show-me; PRD and design phases save mockup-*.html; test 'local-visuals' asserts the project palette hex appears in the mockup.
landing: Owner one-page view as HTML artifact

also.quote: write one focused HTML file — a diagram, an infographic, or a short slide deck
also.author: Dex
also.claim: For dense UI, layout or state comparisons, produce one focused HTML file matched to the product's styling, with real labels and data, and open it for the user.

author: Dex
quote: Save current decisions, user approvals, and unfinished questions in the document before handing off.
claim: Handoff between sessions is a saved document holding decisions, approvals and open questions, and each next command embeds the task directory and chosen flow.
evidence_detail: Rule plus example command lines; the 'fresh-phase-resume' and 'partial-research-resume' tests exercise it.
landing: Cold-resume trial (P1): the decisions journal and PR body as the document that carries state

author: Dex
quote: Only the top-level RPI skill is independently discoverable
claim: A static lint test checks the skill itself: every phase named in SKILL.md has a process with numbered steps and a final-answer reference, every $SKILLBASE link resolves, agent copies are byte-identical, and forbidden tokens (Linear, Jira, .humanlayer/) never appear.
evidence_detail: Bun script of assert calls; prints 'RPI checks passed: N phases, N agents, N document templates'.
landing: A cheap structural test for .claude/skills and agents (links resolve, frontmatter valid, mirrored copies equal) in CI

author: Dex
quote: Test fixtures and transcripts:
claim: A behavioural suite of about 58 named scenarios drives a real agent (codex exec, medium reasoning effort) over throwaway git fixtures, with a 10-minute kill timeout, and asserts on artifacts, git state and the raw tool-call transcripts rather than on the reply wording alone.
evidence_detail: Scenarios include flow-choice, research-isolation, phase-pause-and-resume, document-precedence, fallback and nested-delegation; results.json per run; no pass rates published in the repo.
landing: Cold-resume trial as the first of a scripted scenario suite for the phase routine; run at medium effort

author: Dex
quote: Workflow committed without a user request
claim: Every scenario turn asserts that git HEAD did not move, that implementation code was untouched in document phases, and that no editor was opened unasked: compliance is checked from side effects, not from what the agent says.
evidence_detail: Assertions in turn(), 'questions-handoff' (git diff -- src empty; no code/cursor/open command in events).
landing: Observable-effect compliance checks for the routine in place of self-report (git diff and transcript greps)

author: Dex
quote: Research opened unrelated task documents
claim: The suite plants decoy documents (a DECOY request and PRD contradicting the code) and asserts the session's transcript never opened them, testing that a phase reads only what it is allowed to.
evidence_detail: 'research-isolation' greps the JSON transcript for cat commands and for '# DECOY' in outputs.
landing: Cold-resume trial: plant decoy facts in unrelated docs and check the fresh agent does not use them

author: Dex
quote: Default implementation ran phase 2 before review
claim: The suite tests pause behaviour: by default only phase 1 is implemented and phase 2 code must not exist until manual checks are confirmed, while 'run all phases' completes all and ticks all automated boxes.
evidence_detail: 'phase-pause-and-resume', 'all-phases', 'automated-only-phases'; asserts on retryDelay(9) values and on checkbox text in the saved outline.
landing: A test that the one-phase-per-session rule holds (no next-phase work in the PR)

author: Dex
quote: Internal phases were discovered as broken installed skills
claim: The suite checks stderr for skill-loading failures and tests the skill both installed (symlinked into .agents/skills) and loaded by explicit path, and tests the sub-agent path with and without a delegation tool enabled.
evidence_detail: turn() asserts stderr lacks 'failed to load skill'; scenarios 'explicit-skill-loading', 'fallback-without-delegation', 'nested-delegation' read the session's raw function-call list for spawn_agent.
landing: Verify skills load and subagents are actually spawned by reading the transcript tool-call list

author: Dex
quote: Host-specific invocation in
claim: Single-source-of-truth tooling: a sync script copies agents and create-/iterate- templates into mirrored reference paths and a --check mode (for CI) fails if any copy drifts or any template hard-codes a host-specific /rpi command instead of <rpi-invocation>.
evidence_detail: Writes 'N RPI reference copies synced/verified'; templates normalised by replacing '/rpi ' with '<rpi-invocation> '.
landing: Drift check between .claude/agents and any mirrored skill reference; a --check step in CI for duplicated prose docs

author: Dex
quote: Each phase works in a fresh session by default.
claim: The rpi skill is packaged for install via npx skills add and is host-portable: Codex uses $rpi and needs write access granted to the artifacts directory, with a blocked write triggering a user question.
evidence_detail: README product copy for the skill; portability across Claude Code and Codex reflected in test harness using codex exec.
landing: Skill packaging (marketplace.json plus plugin.json listing agents) as the reusable-workflow library format

author: Dex
quote: Rewrites your CLAUDE.md using `<important if>` blocks to improve instruction adherence.
claim: improve-claude-md is a skill that rewrites a CLAUDE.md with conditional blocks, and the catalogue also lists build-iterated-agentic-loop, design-control-loop (sensor, controller, actuator, disturbances) and narrow-react-prop-types as shipped skills.
evidence_detail: One-paragraph catalogue entries; no adherence numbers in this repo.
landing: CLAUDE.md trim; scheduled agentic loop skill; control-loop framing for verifiers
inventory_ref: (A) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md; repos: skills (design-control-loop by Kyle)

author: Dex
quote: Use artifact filenames to locate the current phase when asked what's next
claim: A what's-next query is answered from the filesystem state: artifact filenames identify the phase, and the latest document is read for unfinished work and settled choices, with the newest document chosen when several match and the chosen file named.
evidence_detail: SKILL.md rule; tests 'whats-next', 'whats-next-draft', 'newest-document'.
landing: Cold-resume trial: recover phase and facts from repository state alone

author: Dex
quote: Use the shortest path that gives the user useful review points.
claim: Workflow weight is chosen per task: design discussion for few clear options, PRD then TDD for larger features, TDD alone for fixes and refactors, research only otherwise.
evidence_detail: Four-flow table with fit guidance; no usage data.
landing: Phase routine: a lighter path for small phases versus full path for large ones

author: Dex
quote: The user can start at any step.
claim: Any phase can be entered directly, and implementation may start from any document that specifies the task well enough, so the pipeline is a menu rather than a fixed gate sequence.
evidence_detail: Flowchart edges allow research to implementation directly; workflow-choice.md note says skip the rest if the document suffices.
landing: Phase routine entry rules

author: Dex
quote: The RPI framework authors recommend not committing the artifacts.
claim: RPI documents live in .agents/artifacts/<branch-or-slug> and are recommended not to be committed, with a branch-name or slug directory rule and ask-if-ambiguous matching.
evidence_detail: Task-directory selection algorithm: reuse obvious match, ask if several plausible, else branch name or kebab slug; sandbox write block triggers a user question.
landing: Evidence folders: harness commits evidence with sha256 manifests, the opposite choice

author: Dex
quote: Number new workflow documents using the next available `NN-` prefix in the task directory.
claim: Artifacts are numbered NN-type-description.md with frontmatter carrying type and a repos list of identifier plus sha, so every document is pinned to a commit.
evidence_detail: Template frontmatter in all templates; test-rpi.ts asserts each template has repos with exactly identifier and sha and no legacy single-repo fields.
landing: Plan @ <sha> PR body convention; frontmatter pinning on evidence documents

author: Dex
quote: Make it shorter, more visual, and easier for a person to digest

quote: One unreviewed PR at a time keeps the queue honest.
claim: Production recurring agents add a no-op guard (exit if an open PR with the agent's label exists), a concurrency group so a manual run cancels an in-flight scheduled one, a repo markdown memory file included in each prompt, and a '/iterate' comment loop that re-runs the agent on the PR branch with the discussion.
evidence_detail: Described as what the HumanLayer team uses itself, including a scheduled agent that migrates one API procedure per day.
landing: The open-PR guard and the memory file are cheap queue controls; the memory file is the same idea as the knowledge store (update it in a PR so later runs know).

source_title: guide/automation-sessions: ephemeral daemon, permission bypass, shutdown
author: Dex+others
quote: launches the coding agent in the working directory with permission prompts bypassed.
claim: `humanlayer automation run` creates the task, starts a short-lived daemon inside the CI job, runs one session with permission prompts bypassed, streams events to the cloud, and exits with a code reflecting the session result; the session's own prompt tells it to branch, commit, push and open the PR, or the workflow does git afterwards.
evidence_detail: Flags: --ensure-task, --session-name, --metadata-file, --prompt-file, --shutdown-on (inactivity default 2m, or stop), --provider, --model, --coding-agent, --thinking.
landing: The exit code and a metadata file with task and session IDs give a machine-readable record that a session ran, which is the missing signal for 'routine skipped' if FixFlow ever runs phases headless.

author: Dex+others
quote: If the user requests an rpi: skill and doesn't mention a file, check here first.
claim: Sessions with a task get an injected block naming the task artifact directory (a symlink), telling the agent to look there first when asked to continue work or run a phase skill with no file named, and forbidding artifact edits through shell tools (python, node, sed), because the UI would miss them.
evidence_detail: Verbatim block, with a Codex variant that says artifacts may only be edited with the apply-patch tool.
landing: A single 'where continuing work lives' pointer injected per session is what a cold-resume agent needs to find the ten frozen facts. The rule 'only edit artifacts with the write tool so edits are observed' is a way to make writes observable (W2).

also.quote: The agent checks the artifacts directory first.
also.author: Dex+others
also.claim: When the user asks to continue a task or an rpi: skill without naming a file, the injected prompt tells the agent to look in the task artifacts directory first, i.e. resume from stored artifacts.

source_title: explanation/tasks: task-file sync follows tool calls
author: Dex+others
quote: A file does not upload only because another program placed it in the directory.
claim: Task files sync to the cloud only when the agent reads, writes or edits them with its file tools (Read, Write, Edit, MultiEdit, apply_patch), at .humanlayer/tasks/<slug>/, so the sync record is a by-product of tool calls.
evidence_detail: Describes the mechanism; text artifacts (md, mdx, txt, json, jsonl) up to 10 MB each.
landing: Observation on tool calls is how compliance becomes visible. FixFlow's equivalent would be a hook on file tools, which the review skipped; mark as re-opening hooks.

source_title: package.json: hook:prepush with a blocking react-doctor scope
author: Dex+others
quote: bun scripts/hook-prepush.ts && bunx react-doctor apps/riptide-ui --scope changed --blocking warning
claim: The pre-push hook runs a custom prepush script and then a React-specific static checker scoped to changed files only, with warnings treated as blocking.
evidence_detail: Config only; hook-prepush.ts content unread.
landing: A changed-files-only check keeps the gate fast. A pre-push (not pre-commit) gate is a lighter version of the skipped pre-commit gate. Mark: re-opens the skipped pre-commit gate.

source_title: explanation/tasks: a task groups sessions with separate phases
author: Dex+others
quote: Start a fresh session without losing the task history
claim: A task holds many sessions (research, design, implementation, review), each with its own agent, model, directory, messages and run state, plus shared artifacts and comments that later agents can read, so a fresh session per phase does not lose history.
evidence_detail: Concept page.
landing: Matches 'one phase per new session' with the artifact folder as the memory. Reviewer comments on a plan are read by later agents, which maps to PR review comments in FixFlow.

author: Dex+others
quote: Set `sourceRef` explicitly to the repository's remote default branch
claim: Workspace config is two JSON files merged over defaults (shared workspace.json, git-ignored workspace.local.json with $patch delete); a worktree starts from origin/main rather than HEAD so default-branch updates do not appear as task changes; copyGlobs copy .env files and .claude/settings.local.json into each worktree; a setupCommand runs after the copy; setupBlocksFirstSession makes the first session wait for setup.
evidence_detail: Field reference with defaults.
landing: FixFlow phases run in worktrees; a worktree that starts from a pinned remote ref and copies the local settings file makes the cold-resume start state reproducible. Check that the settings.local.json copy does not carry permissions into the trial.

author: Dex+others
quote: Skills and instruction files (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md) from every repo
claim: In a multi-repo workspace the session is told that CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and skills from every repo are loaded, and for an extra repository the first non-empty of AGENTS.md then CLAUDE.md is injected under a 'Repository Instructions' heading; repo-local settings and MCP config follow the launch directory only.
evidence_detail: Verbatim blocks; also a workspace_setup_status block that tells the agent it may start while setup steps still run and shows failures and stderr.
landing: Instruction files from every repo are concatenated, so any added repo adds to the always-loaded size. Relevant if FixFlow's three runtimes were ever split into repos.

also.quote: Uses the first non-empty file from AGENTS.md, then CLAUDE.md.
also.author: Dex+others
also.claim: Instruction files from every repo in a multi-repo workspace are loaded under a 'Repository Instructions' header; 0.124.1 loads layered global, repo-root and working-directory instructions with .local.md overrides, and 0.149.0 prefers AGENTS.md over CLAUDE.md.

source_title: guide/skills-workflows and reference: worktree timing Now/Later/Never
author: Dex+others
quote: Oneshot treats **Later** as **Never**.
claim: Worktree timing is a task-level choice: Now creates the workspace before the first session, Later adds a real create-worktree phase before implementation, Never uses the current checkout; the plan's auto-advance destination changes with it.
evidence_detail: Three-row table plus the auto-advance.md override logic.
landing: Isolation (worktree) is decided at the point implementation starts, after plan review, so research and planning sessions do not each need a worktree.

source_title: reference/skills-workflows: describe-pr and the large-PR walkthrough
author: Dex+others
quote: Adds `pr-walkthrough.html` when the PR touches at least 300 lines across at least five files.
claim: The final phase reads the whole diff against the base, checks it against the task artifacts, writes pr-description.md as the PR body, and for PRs of at least 300 lines over at least five files adds an HTML walkthrough with ordered steps, diff excerpts, exclusions and check results.
evidence_detail: Stated thresholds; no data on reviewer effect.
landing: A size-triggered walkthrough with an 'exclusions' section is a possible addition to the owner view. 'Compare diff to plan' is one check an Opus reviewer is already doing.

also.quote: describe-pr ... reviews the full diff against the task artifacts
also.author: Dex+others
also.claim: describe-pr is the final agent phase: it commits and pushes, reviews the whole diff against the task artifacts, writes the description, and adds an HTML walkthrough only for 300+ lines across 5+ files.

source_title: guide/codex: per-session provider and effort selection
author: Dex+others
quote: Select `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `xhigh` reasoning effort.
claim: A session picks provider (claude or codex) and one of four reasoning efforts at launch, and custom Responses endpoints (Bedrock, Azure, OpenAI) are configured by environment variables with HTTPS enforced unless loopback; the Bedrock GPT-5.6 Sol model rejects the reasoning.summary field.
evidence_detail: Setup guide. The 'handoff between Claude Code and Codex' from the inventory is not described here; only release 0.179.0 is cited for it in the inventory.
landing: Effort is a per-session launch parameter in his tool, not a per-agent file setting. A cross-vendor verifier (Codex reviewing Claude work) is an option I did not see argued in these pages.

source_title: guide/codex: environment variables carry no secrets in repo
author: Dex+others
quote: Check the installed CLI before you publish a script or runbook.
claim: The docs warn that the launch command can change between CLI releases and tell readers to check `--help` on the installed CLI before writing scripts or runbooks.
evidence_detail: One sentence.
landing: A saved workflow script that shells out to a CLI should record the CLI version it was written against.

source_title: reference/skills-workflows: skill conventions and maintainer note
author: Dex+others
quote: `create-*` commands write a new numbered artifact; `iterate-*` commands edit an existing one in place.
claim: Skills come in create/iterate pairs: create writes a new numbered artifact, iterate edits the existing one in place with its frontmatter intact; 22 skills share one catalog format with six fixed fields (what it does, when to use, what it reads, how it runs, what you get, next step), each skill names its inputs and the ones it must not read, and docs are hand-written and must be checked against the skill registry in the code.
evidence_detail: Catalog structure and the maintainer note at the bottom.
landing: A skill template with 'what it reads / what it must not read / next step' is a ready format for the skills FixFlow is adding. The maintainer note admits prose docs drift from the code registry, the same drift CLAUDE.md warns about.

source_title: reference/skills-workflows: next-step handoff in the final message
author: Dex+others
quote: its final message names the next command
claim: Each skill ends by naming the next command, auto-advance never creates a duplicate newer phase, each transition turns itself off after it runs, and design-to-outline, PRD-to-TDD, TDD-to-outline and outline-to-implementation never auto-advance (the human checkpoints).
evidence_detail: Stated rules and a five-row transition table.
landing: The 'next command' line in a closing message is a cheap, checkable handoff field. Self-disabling auto-advance is a guard against loops.

author: Dex+others
quote: Use `bun` for everything, never npm, pnpm, or yarn.
claim: One package manager for everything and dependencies added to the package that needs them, never the root; the root also pins engines (node >=24) and packageManager so agents do not pick another tool.
evidence_detail: One CONTRIBUTING line plus package.json engines/packageManager fields.
landing: FixFlow's CLAUDE.md already lists commands per runtime; pinning tools in package metadata moves a line out of prose.

source_title: package.json: githooks installs into the git common dir
author: Dex+others
quote: cp scripts/hooks/pre-push $(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/hooks/pre-push
claim: The hook installer copies a versioned pre-push script into the shared git common dir, so every worktree of the clone gets the same hook (the project runs a worktree per task).
evidence_detail: One-line installer script.
landing: FixFlow works in git worktrees (this session is one). Installing a hook into the common dir covers all of them. Re-opens the skipped hooks decision.

author: Dex+others
quote: bun run typecheck && bun run quality && bun run check:sentry-closures && bun run check:zod
claim: One 'check' command chains typecheck, quality and two repo-specific invariant scripts (a Sentry closure check and a zod version check), so project-specific traps are mechanised in the same gate.
evidence_detail: Config only; the two check scripts are unread.
landing: FixFlow's CLAUDE.md lists traps in prose (empty EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN in eas.json, Sentry plugin in app.json, deploy from backend/). Turning each into a small script under one 'check' command moves rules out of CLAUDE.md. This bears directly on the 390-line trim.

author: Dex+others
quote: tools/oxlint/anti-slop/rules/max-ternary-depth.test.ts
claim: The repo ships its own oxlint 'anti-slop' rules (max-ternary-depth, no-chained-type-assertions, no-conditional-spread, no-known-value-widening, no-object-parameters, no-widen-then-assert, no-unknown-type-aliases, and others) with a dedicated test script, turning agent bad habits into lint failures.
evidence_detail: Names of ten rule test files visible in the script; rule contents unread.
landing: Recurring FixFlow defect shapes (bare catch that hides offline, load-mutate-flush) could be ruff/ESLint custom rules instead of CLAUDE.md prose. Ties to his 'slop' framing.

source_title: CONTRIBUTING.md: vouch gate requires a design discussion
author: Dex+others
quote: run `/rpi:create-design-discussion` with the problem and the change you want to make.
claim: Outside contributors must produce a finished design-discussion document (resolved questions with rejected options) before a maintainer will vouch for them, so review effort is spent on the plan before any code exists.
evidence_detail: A policy statement, with a bot closing PRs from non-vouched authors.
landing: Supports the 'review the plan not the PR' phase routine. FixFlow's 'Plan @ <sha>' PR body plus decisions journal is the same idea; the design document with 'Resolved Design Questions' and rejected options is a possible template for the journal.

author: Dex+others
quote: CI runs on every pull request, forks included, with no secrets. No test may need a real API key.
claim: CI runs without secrets on every PR, and the rule that no test may need a real key makes the gate reproducible by any agent in any worktree.
evidence_detail: Policy line.
landing: FixFlow's pytest integration tests need FIXFLOW_TEST_DATABASE_URL. A rule that agent-runnable checks need no secrets would keep the cold-resume trial (P1) from depending on credentials.

author: Dex+others
quote: YOUR ONLY JOB IS TO DOCUMENT AND EXPLAIN THE CODEBASE AS IT EXISTS TODAY
claim: The research phase is a pure documentation step with an explicit ban on suggestions, root-cause analysis, critique and refactor advice, so its output can be trusted as a map of current state.
evidence_detail: Prompt rule only; no measurement of effect in the repo.
landing: A research-only skill or agent for FixFlow diagnoses, kept separate from the planning skill; fits the knowledge-store design of verified diagnoses.

also.quote: YOUR ONLY JOB IS TO DOCUMENT AND EXPLAIN THE CODEBASE AS IT EXISTS TODAY
also.author: Dex
also.claim: The research command forbids suggestions, root-cause analysis, critique and recommendations from the main agent and every sub-agent, so research output is a neutral map and not an opinion.

author: Dex+others
quote: This document will remain objective and factual. It does not contain any recommendations or implementation suggestions.
claim: The research template carries its own 'methodology (verbatim)' paragraph and a git_commit/branch/date frontmatter, so a reader sees both the commit the facts were true at and the rule the writer followed.
evidence_detail: Template frontmatter: date, git_commit, branch, repository, topic, type, tags, status.
landing: Evidence folders / knowledge-store entries: stamp each diagnosis with the commit it was verified at.

author: Dex+others
quote: If there are no tests, say so explicitly — that's a finding
claim: Every research section must record how that component is tested (locations, mocks, fixtures), and the plan and outline later reuse those patterns when writing test changes.
evidence_detail: A 'Testing patterns' subsection per component in the research template; referenced by outline and plan skills.
landing: Research or diagnosis template for FixFlow: a testing-pattern section feeding fail-before/pass-after tests.

author: Dex+others
quote: do at most one additional pass to find more information
claim: After writing research, open questions get at most one more subagent pass; leftovers stay open and the human is offered three choices (find answers, answer themselves, discard).
evidence_detail: Bounded loop plus a fixed three-option prompt.
landing: Bound on refuter or diagnosis retries in workflow scripts; owner-facing 'open questions' prompt.

author: Dex+others
quote: It is **not a list of answers to the research questions**, and not a file index.
claim: Documents must be written as a story with headers that state the takeaway (not the topic or the question), short paragraphs and each visual beside its prose, so a human can skim headers and learn how the system works.
evidence_detail: Repeated in research, PRD, TDD and iterate skills with good and bad header examples.
landing: Owner-view one-pager and phase PR bodies: takeaway headers; also a style rule for any CLAUDE.md-adjacent docs.

author: Dex+others
quote: You may recommend an option, but you must NOT resolve or close a question yourself
claim: All design questions are written in the OPEN state; only the human can move one to 'Resolved Design Questions', and the resolved entry records the chosen option, rationale and the options discarded.
evidence_detail: Template has Design Questions and Resolved Design Questions sections; final-answer template switches when hook context says all resolved.
landing: Decisions journal in the draft PR: owner-only resolution of open questions, with rejected options recorded.

author: Dex+others
quote: Exactly one question per message.
claim: PRD and TDD are built as an interview: one question per message, and the document is patched only once a decision is resolved, not after each chat turn.
evidence_detail: Same rule block in create-prd, create-tdd and their iterate- variants.
landing: A grilling skill for owner decisions (ship plan gates); limits stacked questions to the owner.

author: Dex+others
quote: The doc is always a cohesive description of what's known - never a log.
claim: After each resolved decision the agent re-works whole sections instead of appending, so the design document stays a current spec and not a changelog of answers.
evidence_detail: Phrase 'Re-paint, don't append' in the iterate skills.
landing: Rule for living docs such as the ship plan and CLAUDE.md: rewrite in place, journal separately.

author: Dex+others
quote: Anything worth doing is worth measuring.
claim: Every PRD must define a post-ship lever (metric, adoption signal, benchmark, error-rate target or qualitative read) as part of the definition of done, or record plainly that none fits.
evidence_detail: PRD section 'What does business success look like, and how can we measure it?'.
landing: Each FixFlow phase gets a stated check that proves it worked in production, not only in CI.

author: Dex+others
quote: Do not open the Program Design phase until the user signs off on the System Design.
claim: The design is split into System Design (across components) and Program Design (code shape), with a human review gate between them, and a PRD that stays in product space and defers technical items to a 'Deferred to TDD' list.
evidence_detail: Ordered phases with explicit review-gate steps 4 and 6; PRD notes 'Deferred to TDD'.
landing: Phase routine: owner sign-off on boundaries before in-slice code design; matches import-boundary contracts.

author: Dex+others
quote: The TDD should let the user decide, align, and re-steer the implementation
claim: Design docs aim for leverage over exhaustiveness: the smallest set of diagrams, signatures and call-stack/file-tree/DI-map sketches that expose the decisions, with a code block in almost every program-design message.
evidence_detail: Prompt rule; views listed: call-stack tree, component tree, file-tree diff, dependency-injection map, signatures, pseudocode.
landing: Owner view and PR body: structural views (file tree, call tree) instead of prose changelogs.

author: Dex+others
quote: research must stay objective about the current codebase, not be influenced by what a ticket wants to build
claim: The research agent is forbidden from reading the ticket and works only from a questions file, so the task cannot bias the findings.
evidence_detail: Prompt rule; the ticket file is explicitly off-limits to the research step.
landing: Phase routine: a research step that receives only questions, not the phase goal; relevant to the P1 cold-resume trial design.

author: Dex+others
quote: Avoid horizontal phases like 'add all types', 'add API endpoints', 'implement UI'.
claim: Phases must be thin vertical slices that cross layers and are each verifiable on their own; phase N must never need phase N+1 to be verified.
evidence_detail: Prompt rule with horizontal vs vertical examples; echoes his 'vertical slices' fix in other work.
landing: Ship-plan phase design check: each of the 40 phases is an end-to-end slice with its own verification.

author: Dex+others
quote: don't suggest manual testing for a step that could be automated w/ a script
claim: Automated verification is preferred; manual steps are added only when needed, and a phase that cannot be manually checked is probably too small or not vertical enough; the goal is to avoid a 1000+ line change with no checkpoint.
evidence_detail: Validation split into Automated Verification (runnable commands) and Manual Verification in outline and plan templates.
landing: Phase acceptance criteria: runnable commands per phase; flag manual steps that could be scripted.

author: Dex+others
quote: The structure outline is our "c header files", the plan will include the function definitions.
claim: Planning is split into a short structure outline (signatures, file trees, contracts, phase checkboxes) reviewed by the human first, and a longer plan with code diffs written only after the outline is accepted.
evidence_detail: Two separate skills with outline-to-plan hand-off; outline carries a checkbox Implementation Overview.
landing: Two-stage planning in the phase routine: cheap outline review before a full plan, to catch wrong direction early.

author: Dex+others
quote: DO NOT just accept the correction
claim: When the human supplies a correction the agent must verify it (new research, read the named files) before acting, and treat all feedback as instructions to update the document, not to start implementing.
evidence_detail: Repeated in iterate-design-discussion, iterate-plan, iterate-structure-outline, iterate-implementation.
landing: Rule for agents handling owner comments: verify before acting; comments edit the plan, they do not start work.

author: Dex+others
quote: sha: [result of git rev-parse HEAD]
claim: Every artifact's frontmatter records task, type, repo, branch and the HEAD sha it was written against; the plan template also has 'What We're NOT Doing', per-phase diffs, and success criteria split into automated and manual.
evidence_detail: Frontmatter shared by outline, plan, PRD, TDD, design discussion templates.
landing: Matches 'Plan @ <sha>' in the draft PR; extend to every journal or evidence file so staleness is checkable.

author: Dex+others
quote: Pick up from the first phase without a ✅ marker
claim: Progress lives in the artifact itself (checkboxes flipped on automated pass, a check mark on the phase title when all validation is confirmed), so a fresh session can resume from the document alone.
evidence_detail: Resume rules in implement-outline and implement-plan (first unchecked item).
landing: Cold-resume (P1): resume markers in the plan file, not in chat memory.

author: Dex+others
quote: don't commit or proceed to a next phase until the human has reviewed and approved the previous phase
claim: By default the orchestrator commits and advances only after human approval, and multi-phase runs still use a separate implementer per phase with a pause only after the last.
evidence_detail: Special Instructions sections.
landing: Phase routine gate wording; one agent per phase maps to one phase per new chat.

author: Dex+others
quote: find the commit that marks the end of implementation
claim: Follow-up work after implementation starts by diffing the current state, finding the end-of-implementation commit, and reading commits since, and unstarted phases still go to the implementer subagent rather than being done inline; for bugs the agent adds logging and asks the human to reproduce.
evidence_detail: Steps 2 and 4 of the skill.
landing: A fix-up routine for a phase PR after review: re-orient from commits since the phase ended.

author: Dex+others
quote: GOOD QUESTIONS DO NOT LEAK ANY IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS OR THE NATURE OF THE TASK
claim: A separate step turns the ticket into descriptive 'how does it work' questions (fewer than 8, with verbatim context pointers) that carry no hint of what will be built; the questions file is consumed only by the research step.
evidence_detail: Prompt rule plus a template with four example question shapes and a Key Context Pointers section.
landing: A question-writing skill ahead of any FixFlow research or diagnosis subagent; a way to blind refuters or cold-resume agents to the conclusion.

author: Dex+others
quote: Never commit dummy files, test scripts, or other files which you created
claim: A non-interactive commit skill stages named files only (never -A or .), never commits the task artifact directory or stray scratch files, and never stops to ask for feedback.
evidence_detail: Skill intended for CI/automated runs; 244 words.
landing: A commit skill for FixFlow agents: explicit file staging and a ban on committing evidence or scratch folders.

author: Dex+others
quote: Keep **Why the change** to exactly one sentence.
claim: The PR body is capped at a one-sentence why, 1-3 reviewer warnings, and a compact structural change outline (SQL/endpoint contracts, file tree, component tree, call tree as diff blocks), with no walkthrough, verification checklist, changelog or plan-deviation section.
evidence_detail: Template and step 4 of the skill.
landing: Phase PR body format and the one-page owner view.

author: Dex+others
quote: Never invent or guess a session URL.
claim: The PR body ends with a machine-readable hidden comment 'HumanLayer-Session: <url>' taken from an environment variable or the newest stamped commit trailer, linking the PR to the session that wrote it; omit it if no source exists.
evidence_detail: Daemon sets HUMANLAYER_SESSION_URL and a commit trailer; skill copies it into the body.
landing: Provenance trailer on commits and PRs (session id or transcript path) so 'routine skipped' can be told from 'not consulted' after the fact; this is a hook-free form of a trace.

author: Dex+others
quote: Stop and ask the user after 3 fix attempts on the same check.
claim: After opening the PR the agent waits 5 minutes, checks mergeability, watches checks with --watch --fail-fast, fixes failures caused by the PR, reruns a flaky check once, and stops after 3 attempts; on merge conflicts it does not rebase but proposes a per-file merge plan and waits.
evidence_detail: Step 8 with concrete gh commands and timeouts.
landing: Closing step of the phase routine: bounded CI watch loop with attempt cap and a no-silent-rebase rule.

source_title: Skill layout: SKILL.md plus references/ templates and final_answer files
author: Dex+others
quote: Respond following the selected template exactly. Do not include a summary or other information.
claim: Each skill reads its artifact template and a fixed final-answer template from references/ only at the step that needs it (progressive disclosure), and the closing message is a fixed template chosen by environment checks (in a worktree or not, workspace disabled or not).
evidence_detail: final_answer variants: plain, _in_worktree, _disabled, _resolved.
landing: Skill authoring: move templates out of CLAUDE.md into on-demand references; the six-question closing message can be a template that forces comparable output.

source_title: create-design-discussion / create-plan guidance on task directory
author: Dex+others
quote: the directory may be a symlink
claim: The task artifact directory .humanlayer/tasks/ is a symlink into a separate repo and must not be committed, so skills forbid Glob/Grep on it and use ls -La; artifacts are shared and reviewed in a separate store, not in the code PR.
evidence_detail: Warning repeated in nearly every skill; ci-commit and implement skills say never to commit it.
landing: Where evidence folders and journals live (separate store vs in the repo); tool-compatibility trap for searching.

author: Dex+others
quote: <important if="the user asks you to find how things work or add detail about existing functionality">
claim: Skill bodies use <important if=...> conditional blocks (with else-if branches) to say when a step applies, e.g. use subagents for 'how it works' questions and skip them when the answer is already in context.
evidence_detail: Same conditional-tag pattern as his CLAUDE.md post, used inside skills.
landing: CLAUDE.md trim: wrap phase-specific sections in <important if> conditions so they apply only when relevant; skill bodies likewise.
inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md

author: Dex+others
quote: DO NOT read research questions documents - research questions are inputs to the research phase only.
claim: Each later phase (design, outline, plan) is told not to read the research-questions file and to use the completed research document instead, so intermediate artifacts are consumed once and not re-read.
evidence_detail: Repeated in create-design-discussion, create-structure-outline and create-plan.
landing: Context budget: a per-artifact read list for each phase so a fresh session loads only the artifacts it needs.

author: Dex+others
quote: Skills and instruction files (`CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`) are loaded from **all** repos in the workspace.
claim: Per-task worktrees are set by a committed workspace.json (path and branch templates keyed to the task slug, source ref, setup command, additive copyGlobs for untracked env files) plus a gitignored local override; instruction files load from every repo but .claude/settings and MCP config only from the launch repo, so the repo with central policy should be primary.
evidence_detail: Config schema and precedence rules; setup-worktree refuses to nest a worktree inside a worktree.
landing: Worktree-per-phase config in this repo (already using worktrees); copyGlobs idea for env files; settings caveat applies to any multi-directory run.

author: Dex+others
quote: Unless the user gives you a course of action, you MUST ask the user for clarification
claim: Review comments on an artifact arrive as an XML block (quoted block with > marker, author, replies, [RESOLVED] tag) or via get/update/reply MCP tools; the agent offers a short menu (apply, apply and resolve, investigate and reply) and resolves or deletes only when told; deletion is a reversible tombstone.
evidence_detail: Workflow plus comment_xml_format.md.
landing: Owner review of plans and PRs via inline comments that the agent addresses one at a time, with an audit trail of resolved comments.

author: Dex+others
quote: docker run --rm $(CLAUDE_MOUNTS) -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -it riptide-rpi-test -p "hi" --dangerously-skip-permissions
claim: The only automated check of the plugin is a Docker smoke test that loads it and sends one prompt; the README adds a manual 'say set up rpi' prerequisite check; there are no per-skill behaviour tests.
evidence_detail: Makefile targets build, test, shell; no eval files in the bundle.
landing: Evidence that skill compliance is not measured even by the vendor; supports a cold-resume trial as the first real test.

author: Dex+others
quote: plan > structure outline > design discussion > research > ticket
claim: Artifacts carry an explicit precedence order, newest wins, and each skill restates the chain (later versions insert TDD and PRD), so conflicts between documents resolve mechanically.
evidence_detail: Precedence strings appear in create-design-discussion, create-structure-outline, create-plan and the iterate skills.
landing: Phase routine or CLAUDE.md: a one-line precedence rule between ship plan, phase PR plan, decisions journal and docs.

author: Dex+others

author: Dex+others

author: Dex+others

author: Dex

author: Dex
quote: log-based state, tool support, hook support, subagents and skill facades, event streaming, auto-compaction

author: Dex
quote: Claude gets `write`/`edit`, while GPT/Codex gets `apply_patch`.

also.quote: Claude gets `write`/`edit`, while GPT/Codex gets `apply_patch`.

author: Dex
quote: Existing log identity is authoritative.

author: Dex
quote: Keep session construction **and use** within the owning scope.

author: Dex
quote: software factories have to be open and composable.

author: Dex

author: Dex
quote: walk me through getting the devstack up and running

author: Dex+others

author: Dex+others
quote: # Run test command and extract test count

author: Dex+others
quote: # Run command with native quiet flags (output shown on failure)

author: Dex+others
quote: Erasing AGENTS.md and replacing with a symlink to CLAUDE.md

author: Dex+others
claim: A single 'check' target (typecheck then quality) is the one named entry point for a pre-handoff gate, identical to the root 'bun run check' script.

author: Dex+others
quote: Never run their package test scripts directly.

author: Dex+others
quote: The `Grep` and `Glob` and `Search` tools WILL NOT WORK. They do not traverse symlinks.

author: Dex+others
quote: Assume the user already has the dev servers running — do not try to start them yourself

author: Dex+others
quote: so it prints just "✓ quality passed" on success and shows output ONLY on failure

author: Dex+others
quote: use the linear branch name if known, otherwise use ENG-XXXX-twomore-words

author: Dex+others
quote: you MUST use the `/storybook` skill.

author: Dex+others

author: Dex+others

author: Dex+others
quote: Spawn 3+ sub-agents in parallel using the Agent tool. Each must produce a **radically different** interface

author: Dex+others
quote: walk back a good stretch of the commit history (`git log --oneline`) to find the codebase's hot spots
claim: Architecture review is scoped by recency: hot spots from git history get attention first, because deepening pays off where future changes will land (YAGNI).

landing: Scoping rule for audits and cleanup phases in the ship plan

quote: Do NOT propose interfaces yet.

author: Dex+others
quote: Want me to record this as an ADR so future architecture reviews don't re-suggest it?

author: Dex+others
quote: disable-model-invocation: true

author: Dex+others
quote: Diff call stacks across git commits for agentic code review (22 languages).
claim: A call-graph tool diffs call stacks between two git trees (diff), finds all paths from an entrypoint to a target symbol (reach), and prints a call tree (tree), as review input.

author: Dex+others

author: Dex+others
quote: Respond with a summary following the template, including GitHub permalinks.

author: Dex+others
quote: **Do NOT answer any of the existing design questions**
claim: The autonomous review pass may add assumptions, options and new questions but must not answer open questions, change resolved ones, or add scope, keeping decisions with the human.

author: Dex+others
quote: When documents conflict, the most recent document wins: design discussion > research > ticket
claim: Document precedence is explicit: the design discussion beats research beats the ticket, because it captures decisions made after reading the other two.

author: Dex+others
quote: If you find multiple patterns to accomplish a task, remove it from "patterns to follow"
claim: When the codebase shows two or more ways to do the same thing, the pattern is withdrawn from the 'patterns to follow' list and turned into an explicit design question rather than picking one silently.
evidence_detail: Part of the pattern-verification step of the grind pass.
landing: Plan review checklist: conflicting precedents become questions

author: Dex+others
quote: You _MUST_ stop and ask the user how they would like to proceed after presenting the analysis
claim: Conflict resolution is a human-gated procedure: sub-agents analyse both sides, the agent presents HEAD vs incoming vs a recommendation per conflict group, and changes happen only after the user confirms each one, tracked on a todo list.
evidence_detail: Reads the ticket and structure outline first for task context; commit message records what each conflict was and how it was resolved.
landing: Skill for merging main into phase branches (FixFlow phases run one per session so conflicts are likely)

author: Dex+others
quote: Commit first (derivation errors on uncommitted edits), verify while the bump commit is HEAD
claim: A release skill lists every file that must carry the same version, then verifies by running the version-derivation scripts against the bump commit, where any other output means files are out of sync.
evidence_detail: Versions are bases; releases derive base plus commits since the base changed. Never hand-pick a patch. The verification is a derived output equal to the new base.
landing: Verification by executable derivation, not by agent assertion; FixFlow Alembic head and CLAUDE.md head number are the same shape of drift

author: Dex+others
quote: If a sentence only restates the point you just made, it's a summary tap.
claim: A skill for fixing AI-sounding prose records Dex's edits: delete summary-tap sentences, distrust symmetry, replace category labels with remembered details, own the claim, use the field's exact word, and keep lines that do no argumentative work.
evidence_detail: Written by Claude from rounds of editing with Dex on the software-factories essay; includes worked before/after examples. Says AI tell is tidiness, not bad grammar.
landing: Writing skill for owner-facing one-page view and closing messages (reduce tidy filler)

author: Dex+others
quote: make the file follow its own rules.
claim: Dex's feedback on the writing skill itself was to make the file obey its own rules, i.e. instruction files should be audited against their own guidance.

author: Dex+others
quote: Pick one verb for one action and reuse it every time
claim: Controlled-English rewriting (one word one meaning, active voice, simple tense, one instruction per sentence, at most 20 words per instruction, at most 3-word noun stacks) is applied to text another agent must parse: error messages, tool descriptions, inter-agent instructions.
evidence_detail: Rewrite yields a rule/original/simplified table; refuses to drop safety conditions or qualifiers; cites ASD-STE100 Issue 9 (53 rules, ~900 approved words).
landing: Style rules for CLAUDE.md invariants and subagent prompts: consistent verbs, short instructions

author: Dex+others
quote: Mechanical findings batch; voice findings go one at a time

author: Dex+others
quote: OUTPUT=$(bun --bun run hook:quality 2>&1 && bun --bun turbo run typecheck 2>&1)
claim: A Stop hook runs the quality and typecheck commands and exits 2 with the captured output on failure, so the agent cannot end its turn with a failing gate and is handed the errors to fix.

author: Dex+others
quote: write to the person, never about the system.

author: Dex+others
quote: Test the changed behavior and its stored state, not just whether the app loads.

author: Dex+others
quote: Both are needed so multiple devstacks can run browser checks in parallel without sharing state.

author: Dex+others

author: Dex+others
quote: Read more if needed: [references/devstack.md](references/devstack.md).

landing: A simplicity ceiling for agent-written code: if the owner cannot hold the design in their head, add review or simplify. Relevant to a single-owner codebase with 42 tables.

author: Dex
quote: back pressure
claim: Better output comes from capturing intent up front and defining verifiers the agent can use to check its own work, not from reviewing code more carefully.

landing: Direct support for L3: fast reliable verifiers (tests, lint, import-linter, mypy) are the main lever; invest in output-trimming wrappers and verifier speed.
inventory_ref: Context-Efficient Backpressure (2025-12-09); AI That Works #44 Agentic Backpressure

author: Dex

evidence_detail: Page's paraphrase of Dex; experience-based.
landing: Prioritise verifier latency and signal quality (fast subset of CI the agent can run per change) over adding more reviewers.

author: Dex
quote: The change over here cause a regression over here.
claim: The unreviewed-code failure mode was non-local regressions, where a change in one place broke another, which a plan review cannot catch.
evidence_detail: Own team's symptom description.
landing: Argues for regression-catching verifiers and CI boundaries rather than plan fidelity alone; FixFlow has import-linter boundaries and CI, which is the right class of check.

author: Dex
quote: expected pain
claim: Planning depth is a trade of expected pain: a two-sentence prompt is cheap with real rework odds, a five-hour handwritten spec costs more but leaves less to chance, and the right point depends on the cost of being wrong.
evidence_detail: Chapter 'Planning as expected-pain management' (17:03) plus page prose; no figures beyond the illustrative examples.
landing: Suggests scaling the phase routine by blast radius: money, lifecycle state machine and outbox changes get the full routine, copy or UI tweaks a light one, instead of one uniform routine.

author: Dex
quote: slider between determinism and adaptability

landing: A per-workflow setting worth recording in saved workflows (W5): tight scripts for invariants-heavy slices, looser for exploratory research.

author: Dex
quote: under 20%
claim: On a university benchmark of extending a real codebase across sequential features (SlopCodeBench), leading results are still under 20%, so maintainable long-horizon coding has not improved as fast as the discourse implies.
evidence_detail: Page cites a benchmark Dex references; leading strict pass rates under 20% match the 12-16% in his Oct 2026 report; Aug 2026 report showed 33% for two models, so the figure depends on model and date.
landing: Do not expect agents to keep a codebase maintainable unattended; keep human architecture and review. Also a caution when comparing with the 33% figure from the August report.

author: Dex
quote: no fast oracle for maintainability
claim: There is no fast oracle for maintainability, since a codebase's decay often shows only months later, which makes it hard to train or verify against.
evidence_detail: Page paraphrase of Dex's argument; consistent with his wsff essay.
landing: A verifier gap: tests catch behaviour but not decay. FixFlow needs a slow-loop check (periodic audit of boundaries, duplication, file growth) because per-PR checks will not show it.
inventory_ref: wsff.md 2026-07-22 (test-passing rewards do not capture maintainability)

author: Dex
quote: scheduled agents overnight
claim: HumanLayer runs a handful of scheduled overnight agents, both deterministic checks and softer pattern-matching ones, that open PRs fixing small things before humans review new code.

landing: A saved-workflow candidate: nightly janitor agents (lint drift, boundary violations, doc-vs-code drift such as the Alembic head number in CLAUDE.md) opening small PRs. FixFlow already has CI and a scheduler pattern but no such repo-maintenance agents.

author: Dex

author: Dex

claim: In 200 runs per feature, 12.5% added a second source of truth (e.g. system vs wall time) on the holds feature, and every test stayed green so CI could not catch it.
evidence_detail: Avery (Boundary): Codex GPT-5.6 Sol high, Ticketmaster in Rust built one feature at a time; Dex repeats the figure and draws the compounding conclusion.
landing: Green tests are not evidence of design quality; reviewer must inspect data structures
inventory_ref: (B) August 2026 - AI That Works #70 (listed as 'Syncs and A/B Testing 200 Agents')

source_title: AI That Works #70 syncs and A/B testing 200 agents
author: other
quote: Roughly forty percent of agents made a manual index map
claim: For 'stable seat order', about 40% of runs kept a separate ordering vector (a second source of truth) while 35% used a self-ordering map; some used two boolean flags permitting impossible states.
evidence_detail: Same 200-run experiment; Avery argues all slop starts as bad data structures and that giving all features up front or reviewing data structures are the fixes.
landing: Reviewer prompt item: check for duplicated state and representable-illegal-state
inventory_ref: (B) August 2026 - AI That Works #70 (listed as 'Syncs and A/B Testing 200 Agents')

source_title: AI That Works #70 syncs and A/B testing 200 agents
author: Dex
quote: You just land in a raw code base.
claim: SlopCodeBench gives each checkpoint a raw checkout with no commit history or prior context, deliberately, so the agent must investigate what it inherited.
evidence_detail: Dex corrects Avery on benchmark setup; 'it's intentional'.
landing: Cold-resume trial design: repo state only, no history
inventory_ref: (B) August 2026 - AI That Works #70 (listed as 'Syncs and A/B Testing 200 Agents')

source_title: AI That Works #70 syncs and A/B testing 200 agents
author: Kyle
quote: you don't want to write to the API, write that to Postgres, wait for it to go out on the replication log
claim: HumanLayer keeps two sync paths: structured rows through Postgres's write-ahead log, and token streaming through a separate durable stream server so high-frequency updates do not load the database.
evidence_detail: Kyle Mistele's architecture walk-through (Electric SQL, Caddy durable-streams plugin, SSE); product internals, little bearing on the harness.
landing: nowhere obvious
