author: Dex+others
quote: Commits every 5-10 minutes with meaningful progress
claim: The developer persona keeps 20+ item TODO lists, commits every 5-10 minutes, and deletes more code than it adds; the rebaser squashes later into a clean history after making a backup branch, and the merger tests after each merge.
evidence_detail: Bulleted persona summaries; rules are in unread persona files.
landing: Frequent small commits plus a separate history-cleanup role; backup-branch-before-rebase as a rule.

author: Dex+others
quote: Follows "read 1500+ lines first" rule to understand context
claim: The 1500-line read rule from his global CLAUDE.md is reused in the developer and merger personas, so it is a shared convention across his tooling, not a one-off.
evidence_detail: Appears twice in the README.
landing: The same rule family as R44-1; shows he repeats rules across files, which cuts against a short CLAUDE.md.

author: Dex
quote: Not every problem needs an agent.
claim: A deterministic script would have done his Makefile-build agent task in 90 seconds; do not use an agent where known steps suffice.
evidence_detail: Own story, two hours of prompt tuning vs a 90-second bash script.
landing: Workflow library: put known fixed sequences in scripts/CI, reserve LLM steps for judgment

author: Dex
quote: most production agents weren't that agentic at all. They were mostly just software
claim: Production agents are mostly deterministic software with LLM steps inserted at the right places.
evidence_detail: Based on conversations with 100+ founders/builders; no counts.
landing: Workflow-tool scripts: deterministic skeleton (gates, CI) with model steps as nodes

author: Dex
quote: Own your control flow
claim: Own the loop (prompt, switch on structured output, context builder, exit conditions) so you can break, summarise, judge and pause in code.
evidence_detail: Design principle (factor 8).
landing: Workflow scripts authored in code with explicit exit conditions; argues for saving them as reusable library

author: Dex
quote: you will always get like tighter, better, higher reliability results by controlling and limiting the number of tokens
claim: Long context windows degrade reliability regardless of model size; keep the context small and focused.
evidence_detail: Appeals to audience experience with 2M-token Gemini.
landing: Supports one-phase-per-session; context budget policy

author: Dex
quote: clear all the air pending errors out. Summarize them.
claim: Own error handling in context: after a valid tool call, clear earlier errors and summarise rather than piling stack traces on the window.
evidence_detail: Observed failure spin-outs; no numbers.
landing: Backpressure scripts: trim failing test/build output to a short summary before it reaches the agent

author: Dex
quote: if you're not looking at every single token
claim: Own your prompts and context format; inspect every token and optimise density and clarity because the only lever on output is input.
evidence_detail: Principle (factors 2-3).
landing: CLAUDE.md and skill text reviewed for token density; supports trimming

author: Dex
quote: small focused agents
claim: Use micro-agents of roughly 3-10 steps inside a mostly deterministic pipeline (their deploy bot), handing back to code afterwards.
evidence_detail: HumanLayer deploy bot; also stated 'less than 100 tools, less than 20 steps' in the MLOps version.
landing: Custom agents and saved workflows as small bounded loops with deterministic gates

author: Dex
quote: find something that is right at the boundary of what the model can do reliably
claim: Value comes from engineering reliability at the frontier of what the model gets right only some of the time.
evidence_detail: Notebook LM example.
landing: Verifier effort should concentrate on failure modes the model sometimes gets wrong

author: Dex
quote: agents should be stateless. You should own the state
claim: Keep the agent as a stateless reducer; persist and own execution and business state outside it so runs can pause, resume and be launched from any trigger.
evidence_detail: Factors 5, 6, 12.
landing: State lives in the repo (journal, evidence folders), not in chat; supports cold resume

author: Dex
quote: Tool use is harmful.
claim: Tool calls are just model-emitted JSON handled by deterministic code; treating tool use as magic obscures control.
evidence_detail: Deliberately provocative framing (factor 4).
landing: None direct

author: Dex
quote: not here to bash frameworks. I would think of this as much as anything as a wish list
claim: Frameworks should be treated as a feature wish-list; 12-factor is a set of requirements for them, not an anti-framework stance (4,000 stars in a month or two; 14 contributors).
evidence_detail: Star and contributor counts as stated at the talk.
landing: Nowhere obvious

author: Dex
quote: Follows "read 1500+ lines first" rule to understand context
claim: Role personas (developer, code-reviewer, rebaser, merger, multiplan-manager) are installed as files and chosen via CLAUDE.md, with rules such as read 1500+ lines first, 20+ item TODO lists, commit every 5-10 minutes, and delete more code than you add.
evidence_detail: README bullet summary of persona rules; no results.
landing: Custom agents: reviewer/merger personas as agent files rather than CLAUDE.md prose; existing Opus reviewer role

source_title: 12-factor-agents factor-03 (added section 'Don't take it from me')
author: Dex
quote: Everything is context engineering.
claim: Dex positions context engineering as the umbrella (prompts, retrieved docs, history, memory, output instructions) and notes the term took off about two months after 12-factor agents, citing Karpathy, Tobi Lutke and a July 2025 cheat sheet.
evidence_detail: Links to third-party tweets as support; no experiment. Added after 2025-06-25 (screenshot date).
landing: nowhere obvious; framing for the knowledge-store design

author: Dex
quote: I always thought of it more as a "wish list"
claim: 12-factor agents is a wish list of what the community wants from agent tools, not a hit piece on frameworks.
evidence_detail: Clarification of intent, anecdotal.
landing: Low relevance to the harness; context on how to read his anti-framework stance.

author: Dex
quote: they're mostly just well-engineered software with LLM capabilities integrated at key points
claim: Successful production AI systems are mostly ordinary well-engineered software with small focused LLM loops inserted, not a prompt plus a bag of tools.
evidence_detail: Based on trying many frameworks and talking to founders; no counts.
landing: Justifies deterministic scripts around agents (saved workflows) rather than free-form agent runs.

author: Dex
quote: you'll ALWAYS get better results with a small, focused prompt and context
claim: Even as context windows grow, a small focused context beats a long one; loops past 10-20 turns become unrecoverable messes.
evidence_detail: Based on conversations with builders; no experiment.
landing: Rationale for one phase per new session; a turn-count ceiling per phase in the routine.
inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

author: Dex
quote: keeping agents focused on specific domains with 3-10, maybe 20 steps max
claim: Keep agents to small scopes of 3-10 (max ~20) steps so context stays manageable.
evidence_detail: Rule of thumb.
landing: Sizing guide for custom agents and workflow steps (the Haiku locator, future skills) and for phase size.
inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

author: Dex
quote: Agents, at least the good ones, are comprised of mostly just software.
claim: Good agent systems are mostly deterministic code with LLM steps at chosen points; own control flow rather than looping until done.
evidence_detail: Observations from founders and his own deploy bot; no numbers.
landing: Supports saving workflows as scripts (deterministic control flow, LLM steps in slots) instead of ad hoc prompts; hooks/scripts over instructions.
inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

author: Dex
quote: Consider hiding errors and failed calls from context window once they are resolved.
claim: Prune resolved errors from context, restructure how errors are represented, and cap consecutive errors (~3) before escalating to a human.
evidence_detail: Code example with errorCounter; no data.
landing: Rule for refuter/verifier loops: a retry cap (3) then escalate to owner; do not keep failed attempts in the next verifier's context.
inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

author: Dex
quote: we need to be able to interrupt a working agent and resume later
claim: Agents must be pausable between tool selection and tool execution so humans can approve high-stakes calls; without it you restrict to low-risk work or yolo.
evidence_detail: Stated as his number one framework feature request; deploybot example.
landing: Approval-gate shape for irreversible steps (railway up, migrations); a hook-based pre-tool approval is the Claude Code analogue (re-opens hooks).
inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

author: Dex
quote: you can engineer your application so that you can infer all execution state from the context window
claim: Unify execution state and business state in one serialisable thread so you can resume, fork, debug, and render it for humans.
evidence_detail: Benefits list: simplicity, serialisation, recovery, forking, observability.
landing: Cold-resume principle: a phase's state should be recoverable from the repo artefacts (journal, PR body) alone, which is what P1's trial tests.
inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

author: Dex
quote: Everything is context engineering. LLMs are stateless functions that turn inputs into outputs.
claim: Output quality depends only on the inputs assembled per call: prompt, retrieved docs, history, memory, output instructions.
evidence_detail: Core thesis of Factor 3.
landing: Framing for the knowledge-store: what a fresh agent knows is only what the store/repo puts in its context.
inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

author: Dex
quote: Own your prompts and treat them as first-class code
claim: Prompts should be owned, versioned and tested with evals like code rather than outsourced to a framework.
evidence_detail: Benefits list: control, testing, iteration, transparency.
landing: Treat skill/agent prompt files and the phase routine as code: versioned, with a test (the cold-resume trial is such a test).
inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

author: Dex
quote: Even as models support longer and longer context windows
claim: Micro agents inside a deterministic DAG make it easy to take human feedback into workflow steps without context error loops; keep scope small now and widen only as reliability allows.
evidence_detail: Real deploy agent example (HumanLayer's own); no numbers.
landing: Design rule for workflow library: deterministic outer script, small agent steps; widen scope only after measured reliability.
inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)

author: Dex
quote: Own Your Control Flow
claim: Own control flow to add summarisation of tool results, LLM-as-judge on structured output, compaction, tracing, rate limiting, and durable waits.
evidence_detail: List of control-flow hooks in Factor 8 with code.
landing: Workflow scripts as the owned control flow: judge panels, tracing of which steps ran (answers 'routine skipped?' from the script log).
inventory_ref: (A3) HumanLayer blog and product posts - 2025-04-03 (listed only)
